$comment: Derived from the committed signed snapshot known-answer/signed-examples/revocation/kat-keypair-001-snapshot.json: the same inner `revocation_list` body and the same committed signature (signed by kat-keypair-001), with `version` changed from `aitp/0.3` to `aitp/9.9` after signing. `aitp/9.9` is chosen because no release will assign it (as in env-010 and man-002). The signature verifies over the original body and not over this one (both checked by scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs and scripts/recompute-known-answer-independent.py), so a verifier that checked the signature first would report REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_SIGNATURE_INVALID. A runner MUST NOT re-mint it. RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5 runs structural validation before any signature work, and the schema's `version` const rejects `aitp/9.9`. The snapshot has no separate version code: VERSIONING.md (Forward / backward compatibility) names REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID as the snapshot's unknown-version code, not the envelope's UNKNOWN_VERSION (aitp-rs#265 reported UNKNOWN_VERSION here).
description: A revocation snapshot whose inner `revocation_list` body declares a `version` the receiver does not implement, changed after signing. RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5: structural validation comes first, before any signature work, and `version` MUST be `aitp/0.3`. Receivers MUST reject with REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID, the revocation snapshot's unknown-version code (VERSIONING.md; registries/error-codes.md, Structural rejection). Expected: REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID, not UNKNOWN_VERSION and not REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_SIGNATURE_INVALID.

expected.rationale: `revocation_list.version` is `aitp/9.9`, which `aitp-revocation-list.schema.json`'s `version` const rejects. RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5 runs structural validation before the signature check, so the code is REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID even though the signature also fails (it was made over the `aitp/0.3` body). UNKNOWN_VERSION is the code for envelopes and JWS-profile artifacts, not for the snapshot.
